text:
Question: The nurse in the community clinic is caring for a 72-year-old client who has heart failure and is taking prescribed spironolactone.
Which of the following should the nurse include in the client’s care plan?
A. Encourage the client to prepare foods using potassium salt substitutes.
B. Reinforce teaching for the client about the low sodium diet.
C. Remind the client to complete all activities of daily living within 1 hour of awakening.
D. Tell the client to walk their dog for no more than 5 minutes per day as the primary exercise modality.
Correct answer: B. Reinforce teaching for the client about the low sodium diet.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Reinforce teaching for the client about the low sodium diet.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Reinforce teaching for the client about the low sodium diet.” – Less sodium reduces fluid retention
Not correct:
• “Encourage the client to prepare foods using potassium salt substitutes.” – Potassium-sparing drug raises hyperkalemia risk
• “Remind the client to complete all activities of daily living within 1 hour of awakening.” – Clusters activity and may increase fatigue
• “Tell the client to walk their dog for no more than 5 minutes per day as the primary exe…” – Exercise should be individualized, not arbitrarily limited
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 8 - Cardiac, slide 39: “Client may be placed on a low sodium diet”
• Unit 8 - Cardiac, slide 8: “Monitor for hyperkalemia”

slides.title: There are 4 chambers of the heart. Which of the following is accurate regarding
text: Question: There are 4 chambers of the heart.  Which of the following is accurate regarding the left atrium?  (Select all that apply.)
A. This chamber sends blood to the left ventricle through the aorta (aortic) valve
B. This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary arteries
C. This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins
D. This chamber pumps blood to the left ventricle
E. This chamber sends blood through the mitral valve
F. This chamber sends blood to the left ventricle through the tricuspid valve
Correct answers: C. This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins; D. This chamber pumps blood to the left ventricle; E. This chamber sends blood through the mitral valve
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins
• This chamber pumps blood to the left ventricle
• This chamber sends blood through the mitral valve
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins” – Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood
• “This chamber pumps blood to the left ventricle” – Left atrium empties into LV
• “This chamber sends blood through the mitral valve” – Mitral valve separates LA and LV
Not correct:
• “This chamber sends blood to the left ventricle through the aorta (aortic) valve” – Aortic valve connects LV to aorta
• “This chamber receives blood from the lungs via the pulmonary arteries” – Pulmonary arteries carry blood away from right ventricle
• “This chamber sends blood to the left ventricle through the tricuspid valve” – Tricuspid valve is right-sided
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a patient who is having issues with their tricuspid valv
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a patient who is having issues with their tricuspid valve. The nurse is explaining to the patient about the tricuspid valve. Which of the following is accurate? (Select all that apply.)
A. The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits between the ventricle and the aorta
B. This valve is also known as the tricuspid valve because it has 3 flaps
C. This valve is open when the heart pumps blood out to the body
D. The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits between the right atrium and the right ventricle
E. This valve is closed when the heart pumps blood out to the body

Correct answers: B. This valve is also known as the tricuspid valve because it has 3 flaps; D. The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits between the right atrium and the right ventricle; E. This valve is closed when the heart pumps blood out to the body
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• This valve is also known as the tricuspid valve because it has 3 flaps
• The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits between the right atrium and the right ventricle
• This valve is closed when the heart pumps blood out to the body
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “This valve is also known as the tricuspid valve because it has 3 flaps” – Three leaflets
• “The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits b…” – Correct right AV valve location
• “This valve is closed when the heart pumps blood out to the body” – Closes to prevent backflow during systole
Not correct:
• “The tricuspid valve is also known as the right atrioventricular valve because it sits b…” – Valve is between right atrium and ventricle
• “This valve is open when the heart pumps blood out to the body” – Closes during ventricular systole
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is preparing to administer an ACE inhibitor to a patient who has hyper
text: Question: The nurse is preparing to administer an ACE inhibitor to a patient who has hypertension. The nurse notes peripheral edema and swelling of the patient’s lips. The patient has a blood pressure of 160/80 mm Hg and a heart rate of 76 beats per minute. What is the nurse’s next action?
A. Administer the dose and observe carefully for hypotension.
B. Notify the provider and request an order for a diuretic medication.
C. Request an order for serum electrolytes and renal function tests.
D. Hold the dose and notify the provider of a hypersensitivity reaction.
Correct answer: D. Hold the dose and notify the provider of a hypersensitivity reaction.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Hold the dose and notify the provider of a hypersensitivity reaction.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Hold the dose and notify the provider of a hypersensitivity reaction.” – Hold ACE inhibitor; evaluate airway urgently
Not correct:
• “Administer the dose and observe carefully for hypotension.” – Giving another dose risks airway swelling
• “Notify the provider and request an order for a diuretic medication.” – Does not treat angioedema
• “Request an order for serum electrolytes and renal function tests.” – Labs do not address immediate airway risk
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

B. Fourth left intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
C. Fourth left intercostal space at the sternal border
D. Fifth left intercostal space at the midclavicular line
Correct answer: D. Fifth left intercostal space at the midclavicular line
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):

(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Fifth left intercostal space at the midclavicular line” – Usual adult PMI location
Not correct:
• “Third left intercostal space at the midclavicular line” – Too superior
• “Fourth left intercostal space at the anterior axillary line” – Too lateral and superior
• “Fourth left intercostal space at the sternal border” – Too medial and superior

slides.title: What should the nurse do when assessing the carotid arteries of an older patient
text: Question: What should the nurse do when assessing the carotid arteries of an older patient with cardiovascular disease?
A. Simultaneously palpate both arteries to compare amplitude.
B. Instruct the patient to take slow deep breaths during auscultation.
C. Palpate the artery in the upper one-third of the neck.
D. Listen with the bell of the stethoscope to assess for bruits.
Correct answer: D. Listen with the bell of the stethoscope to assess for bruits.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Listen with the bell of the stethoscope to assess for bruits.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Listen with the bell of the stethoscope to assess for bruits.” – Bell detects low-pitched vascular bruit
Not correct:
• “Simultaneously palpate both arteries to compare amplitude.” – Bilateral pressure can reduce cerebral perfusion
• “Instruct the patient to take slow deep breaths during auscultation.” – Breath sounds interfere with bruit assessment
• “Palpate the artery in the upper one-third of the neck.” – Avoid carotid sinus pressure
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: A patient is ordered to receive a nitrate to relieve stable angina. What side effect(s) will the nurse anticipate in a patient receiving this medication?
A. Increased blood pressure
B. Pounding headache
C. Nausea and vomiting
D. Pruritus and skin rash
Correct answer: B. Pounding headache
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):

• “Nausea and vomiting” – Possible but less typical
• “Pruritus and skin rash” – Not characteristic nitrate effect

text: Question: A patient has congestive HF and has been taking digoxin for 9 years. The patient is admitted with signs and symptoms of digoxin toxicity. Which signs and symptoms are associated with digoxin toxicity? (Select all that apply.)

notes: Rationale:

slides.title: The nurse working on a step-down unit has just received report on the following
text: Question: The nurse working on a step-down unit has just received report on the following patients.  The nurse should first assess the patent with
A. stable VS who returned 40 min ago after a PTCA.
B. angina whose chest pain was relieved by two nitroglycerin tablets taken two hours ago.
C. angina currently, nausea and increased anxiety.
D. complaints of a headache who was transferred from CCU earlier after recovering from a MI.
Correct answer: C. angina currently, nausea and increased anxiety.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• angina currently, nausea and increased anxiety.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “angina currently, nausea and increased anxiety.” – Current angina with nausea may indicate acute ischemia
Not correct:
• “stable VS who returned 40 min ago after a PTCA.” – Recent PCI requires monitoring but stable vital signs listed
• “angina whose chest pain was relieved by two nitroglycerin tablets taken two hours ago.” – Pain resolved earlier
• “complaints of a headache who was transferred from CCU earlier after recovering from a MI.” – Assess headache after acute ischemic concern

text: Question: A patient has been prescribed cilostazol. Which statement by the client indicates the need for further teaching?
A. “This medication is used to improve blood flow.”
B. “I can continue to take ginkgo biloba to improve my memory.”
C. “I can take the medication with food if it causes nausea.”
D. “I should be cautious when standing.”
Correct answer: B. “I can continue to take ginkgo biloba to improve my memory.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “I can continue to take ginkgo biloba to improve my memory.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““I can continue to take ginkgo biloba to improve my memory.”” – Ginkgo may increase bleeding risk
Not correct:
• ““This medication is used to improve blood flow.”” – Increases walking distance via vasodilation and antiplatelet effects
• ““I can take the medication with food if it causes nausea.”” – Food timing actually should follow label; take on empty stomach
• ““I should be cautious when standing.”” – Drug can cause dizziness

text: Question: A client who was admitted with a myocardial infarction experiences a 15-second episode of ventricular tachycardia, then converts to sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 98 beats/minute. Which of the following actions should the nurse take next?
A. Document the rhythm and continue to monitor the client.
B. Prepare to start IV Heparin protocol.
C. Obtain stat cardiac enzymes
D. Prepare to give IV amiodarone
Correct answer: A. Document the rhythm and continue to monitor the client.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Document the rhythm and continue to monitor the client.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
